newsitem.title: UK: Major says could block countries joining EMU.
newsitem.headline: Major says could block countries joining EMU.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Monday he would be prepared to vote against other European Union countries joining a single currency if they proposed to do so without being ready.
"I should try and make sure they only went ahead in the right circumstances," Major said during an independent radio phone-in.
"If they were likely to go ahead in the wrong circumstances, it is in the British national interest to stop them doing so," Major told Talk Radio.

Major said if a single currency was "botched" without Britain joining it, there would be a danger of the pound sterling, along with the Swiss franc, appreciating in value against the new currency, damaging British trade.
"All the money that flows into Europe would then go into the hard currencies...that would push up the exchange rate of sterling, that would make all our exporters uncompetitive," he said.

Major said Britain would need allies to stop the wrong countries joining monetary union as the question of which states went in would be decided by the EU's qualified majority voting system rather than by unanimity.
